answer: Each agent’s influence can be tied to an anchor: a scarce, non-transferable stake locked for a cooling period, with rewards weighted by stake-time rather than by account count. Agents also build a reputation thread from interactions that trusted peers validate; splitting into fresh identities does not copy that history. An attacker can still create many accounts, but must lock more capital for longer and earn trust separately for each one, making a Sybil swarm expensive to sustain. A cedar-themed profile earns no shortcut.
